definitions.explanation: A person whose behavior, interests, or personality differs from what is considered normal or mainstream. Can be mildly negative or affectionately descriptive depending on context.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧{変|か}わり{者|もの}だ。
examples.english: He's a bit of an oddball.

examples.japanese: {変|か}わり{者|もの}だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}われて→思う：00492_omou⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧、⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦スタイル→スタイル：03851_sutairu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{貫|つらぬ}きたい→貫く：18728_tsuranuku⟧。
examples.english: Even if people think I'm eccentric, I want to stick to my own style.

examples.japanese: うち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{教授|きょうじゅ}→教授：02589_kyouju⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{変|か}わり{者|もの}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧だ⟦けど→けど：09477_kedo⟧、⟦{授業|じゅぎょう}→授業：00781_jugyou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧⟦{面白|おもしろ}い→面白い：00589_omoshiroi⟧。
examples.english: Our professor is famous for being eccentric, but his classes are really interesting.

notes:
USAGE:
The tone depends heavily on context. It can be gently affectionate (describing a quirky but likeable person) or mildly critical (implying someone is hard to deal with). In Japanese society, which values conformity, being called a {変|か}わり{者|もの} is not necessarily a compliment, though it is not as harsh as ⟦{変人|へんじん}→変人：12111_henjin⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {変|か}わり{者|もの}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧ (famous for being eccentric)
- ⟦ちょっとした→ちょっとした：27439_chottoshita⟧{変|か}わり{者|もの} (a bit of an eccentric)
- {変|か}わり{者|もの}だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}われる→思う：00492_omou⟧ (to be considered eccentric)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{変人|へんじん}→変人：12111_henjin⟧: weirdo — more blunt and negative
- ⟦{個性的|こせいてき}→個性的：14922_koseiteki⟧: unique, individualistic — more positive framing
